newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes fall, buying dries up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes fall, buying dries up.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices fell Tuesday, as excess imports weakened West Texas Intermediate (WTI) and discounts flattened on a lack of buying interest, traders said.
Spot trading was light, with many traders flush with supply after two months of refinery maintenance shutdowns.
"Most people are full so they'll run inventories before they go out and buy," a buyer said.
The large number of imports into U.S. Gulf refiners helped push down April WTI 35 cents, widening the contango between April and May cargoes 20 cents, traders said.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude fell to $19.25/19.45 a barrel. The bellwether western grade remains discounted -$0.80 cents off WTI, with the last deal done Thursday.
BP Oil declined to offer a price for ANS again Tuesday, with buyers saying the region's main seller waited to see if Gulf imports would come through the Panama Canal.
In other light markets, Line 63 stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, with a significant-sized cargo sold at $1.00 over postings Monday.
With WTI prices continuing to fall, traders said California oil companies may shed Friday's 50-cent increase for heavy grades.
